chunks: And it has been narrated from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Aʿraj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

Indeed, Quraysh in the Jāhiliyyah demolished the House. Then when they wanted to build it, they were prevented from it, and terror was cast into their hearts, until one of them said: Let every man among you bring the best of his wealth, and do not bring wealth that you acquired from severing kinship ties or from what is haram. So they did that, and they were left free to build it, and they built it.

Until they reached the place of the Black Stone, then they disputed over it as to which of them would place the Stone in its place, until it nearly became an evil conflict among them. So they agreed to appoint as judge the first one who would enter from the gate of the mosque. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entered. When he came to them, he called for a cloth and spread it out, then placed the Stone in its middle. Then the tribes took hold of the sides of the cloth and raised it. Then he عليه السلام took it and placed it in its position.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, singled him out with it.

key_terms.ٱلرُّعْبُ: fear or terror cast into their hearts
key_terms.ٱلْبَيْتَ: the Kaʿbah, the Sacred House in Makkah
key_terms.ٱلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: the pre-Islamic period before the advent of Islam
key_terms.ٱلْحَجَرِ ٱلْأَسْوَدِ: the Black Stone set into the Kaʿbah
key_terms.ٱلْقَبَائِلُ: the tribes of Quraysh involved in the dispute

ai.seo_question: How did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله resolve the dispute over the Black Stone during the rebuilding of the Kaʿbah?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the rebuilding of the Kaʿbah by Quraysh and how they were only enabled to continue after resolving to use pure wealth, not wealth gained through severing kinship ties or haram means. It also describes how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله peacefully resolved the dispute over placing the Black Stone, a distinction by which Allah عز وجل honored him.
